title: CRLR/344/2018 of LAVEER SINGH RANA Vs SMT. DEEPMALA

paras.text:
CRLR No.344 of 2018
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
 Mr. Deep Prakash Bhatt, Advocate for the
revisionist.
Mr. V.D. Bisen, Advocate for the private respondent
nos.1 and 2.
Mr. P.S. Bohra, AGA for the State of
Uttarakhand/respondent no.3.
This is a Criminal Revision where the revisionist has
challenged the order dated 27.07.2018 as passed on an
application under Sub Section (2) of Section 125 of Cr.P.C.
being Case No.523 of 2017, Smt. Deepmala vs. Laveer
Singh Rana, wherein the Family Court while allowing the
application for an award of interim maintenance has
directed the remittance of Rs.5,000/- per month as interim
maintenance to the revisionist no.1 as well as revisionist
no.2 i.e. her daughter which has been directed to be made
payable by 10th of each month.
As per the order sheet, it shows that in this case was
having lot of contradictory stands taken by the revisionist
before this Court particularly, the reference may be had to
the proceedings as held by this Court on 04.04.2019. On
04.04.2019 in a pre session of the proceedings, the matter
was referred to the mediator for an adjudication, the
mediator submitted the report on 04.04.2019 giving the
following report:-
"The criminal revision filed against the
judgment and order dated 27.07.2018 passed by the
Learned Judge of Family Court, District Udham
Singh Nagar Application no.523 of 2017 "Smt.
Deepmala vs. Laveer Singh" under Section 125
Cr.P.C. P.S. Khatima, District Udham Singh Nagar
whereby the Learned Judge of Family Court
awarded maintenance for Rs.5,000/- to the
respondent no.1 and her daughter
During the course of mediation the parties
are settled the dispute and decided to live together,
the mediation proceedings is closed as successful.
The terms and conditions of the settlement is the
part of this report may be placed on record.
Let a report to this effect be submitted to the
Hon'ble Court.
Mediation Successful."
As a consequence of stand taken by the revisionist
the mediation was successfully concluded subject to the

terms contained therein as quoted above. Based on the said
mediation report and in the presence of both the parties, the
mediation was settled in terms of the following conditions:-
"During the course of mediation the parties are settled
as follows-1. Laveer Singh Rana submitted that Smt.
Deepmala Rana should not be violent with
his family members as in past during scuffle,
she bit her mother in law so deep that the
middle finger of left hand was cut.
2. Both the parties has committed that there
will be no violence.
3. Laveer Singh Rana has already filed Divorce
case in Family Court. Smt. Deepmala Rana
will move applications through her lawyers
to withdraw the mentioned cases. Smt.
Deepmala Rana and Laveer Singh Rana will
move applications next week in the court
below to withdraw their respective cases.
4. After that Smt. Deepmala Rana with her
daughter will go with her husband Laveer
Singh Rana at her matrimonial house village
Bhurya Tharu, P.S. Khatima, District
Udham Singh Nagar.
5. That this settlement and agreement made
between the parties with freewill without ill
will, influence, fear and favour, with free
mind of the parties in presence of their
respective counsel.
6. The parties have liberty to move application
before the appropriate forum if any of them
do not fulfill the above terms and conditions.
Let a report to this effect be submitted to the
Hon'ble Court."
These conditions of settlement were duly signed by
the revisionist, the private respondent no.1 and their
respective counsel. Since the same was not adhere to and
despite of the fact that compromise was already arrived at
between the parties, the Coordinate Bench of this Court
anticipating a positive response in terms of the settlement
has quashed the order determining the interim maintenance.
That too was done by an order passed on 04.04.2019 on
culmination of the mediation proceedings.
Later on, a misc. application was filed by the counsel
for the revisionist being Misc. Application No.312 of 2019,
on which the revisionist was expected to appear through his
previous counsel, but he had not participated in the

proceedings and in consequence thereto, the Coordinate
Bench of this Court had passed an order on 27.11.2019 and
thereby had recalled the order dated 04.04.2019 quashing
the order of interim maintenance, which is impugned in the
present Criminal Revision.
The conduct and diligence with which the revisionist
has taken the proceedings of the court including those
before the Hon'ble High Court, this Court is of the view
that such a conduct of the revisionist is deplorable and no
solace as such is required to be extended for such type of a
litigant, who does not stand to his convictions, particularly
the one made before court of law, which has been arrived at
between the parties as reflected from the order dated
04.04.2019. In such an eventuality, after having gone
through the impugned order under challenge, whereby the
Family Court has determined the interim maintenance by
allowing the application paper no.7 Ga granting interim
maintenance to the tune of Rs.5,000/- per month directed to
make payable to the respondent nos.1 and 2 by 10th of each
month. This Court is of the view that the impugned does
not suffer from any apparent error, because the matrimony,
the birth of the child, the desertion and the income accruing
to the revisionist are the facts, which stand concluded by
finding of facts and in such an eventuality the revisionist
owes a responsibility to maintain his wife and the daughter,
hence this Court has got no other option at this stage,
except to dismiss the revision and affirm the impugned
order dated 27.07.2018, directing the revisionist to pay the
maintenance as determined by 10th of each month and
arrears are directed to be paid to respondent no.1 within a
period of three months from the date of the application.
The revision lacks merit and the same is dismissed
accordingly.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) 05.12.2019
